- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.73) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model underestimates prices; increase forecast modestly to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently overpredicts prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 70.91 → 71.42) — apply downward correction of 1–2% for such periods.
- Model underpredicts prices during prolonged downward trends — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often peaks 1–2 days after true price peaks — shift forecast peak backward by 1–2 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- Model frequently overcorrects after minor price drops — reduce forecast magnitude by 0.3–0.8% for consecutive low sentiment days.
